title: src → cli — the new Python project root

meta.subtitle: Rename src/ to cli/ and move all Python toolchain files inside. Kit stays the core runtime at the top level.
meta.summary: Confirmed rename: cli/ becomes the Python project root (package + tests + pyproject + bin + lockfile). kit/ is the actual core runtime; nothing under cli/ is ‘source’ in the system-architecture sense, so the directory should not be named src/. Trade is real (Python tools assume src/) — accepted, with explicit overrides.

blocks.summary: ‘src’ implies the project's source-of-truth — but the kit (chrome.js + chrome.css + renderer.js + schemas + glossary) is the actual core. The CLI is a toolchain, not the source. Rename src/ to cli/, move pyproject.toml + bin/html-doc + uv.lock + tests inside, and the repo's shape finally matches the system: kit/ at the top because it IS the system; cli/ at the same level because it's a sibling tool.
bullets: Rename src/ → cli/ — directory name now matches contents.
Move pyproject.toml, uv.lock, bin/html-doc into cli/ — cli/ is the Python project root.
Top-level repo shape becomes: kit/ (core) · cli/ (toolchain) · docs/ (content) · examples/ — each name says what's inside.
Python ecosystem overrides accepted explicitly — hatchling, ruff, pytest, mypy configs declare cli/ as the source dir.
Install command becomes ‘uv tool install ./cli’ — surfaced in README + CI.

blocks.title: Why the rename — restated
blocks.lead: The previous draft of this plan argued against the rename on Python-ecosystem-cost grounds. That misread the priority. Clarity of repo structure is the goal; the tool overrides are the price.

cards.title: What ‘src/’ implies
items: ‘src’ = source root = where the project's core lives.
In this repo, that's *not* what's under src/ — only the CLI toolchain lives there.
The actual core (chrome.js, chrome.css, renderer.js, schemas, glossary, extrefs) lives in kit/.
Result: a reader entering the repo via src/ has been pointed at the wrong thing.

cards.title: What ‘cli/’ implies
items: ‘cli’ = command-line toolchain.
Matches exactly what's under it: argparse, build, serve, check, init, clean.
Pairs cleanly with kit/ at the same level — both directory names describe their contents.
‘kit/’ keeps its identity as the core; ‘cli/’ becomes the sibling tooling.

blocks.title: The reframe
blocks.content: The previous draft treated this as ‘src/ is conventional, cli/ would need config overrides’. The real framing: the kit is the system, the CLI is one of several possible front-ends to it (today: CLI; tomorrow maybe: a VS Code plugin, a server, a publish bot). cli/ is the natural home for the current front-end; future front-ends would live as siblings (vscode/, server/, …). ‘src/’ implies a single source-of-truth — the kit already is that, just at the top level.

blocks.title: Layout — before / after
blocks.lead: Side-by-side. Same set of files; the regrouping is what tells the reader the system shape.

│   │   └── templates/              │   └── extrefs/

blocks.title: The shape the reader now sees
blocks.content: Three top-level work directories: kit/ (what ships to readers), cli/ (what builds + serves), docs/ (what describes the kit using the kit). README.md + CLAUDE.md + LICENSE alone at the root. No more ‘which of these is the source?’ ambiguity — kit is the source, cli is the toolchain.

blocks.title: What moves, what stays
blocks.lead: Exhaustive list — anything touching Python goes inside cli/.

rows: The Python package — directory rename is the headline of this whole plan.
Python project metadata belongs with the Python code, not at a top level shared with the kit.
The PEP 723 shim is a CLI launcher — it lives with the CLI.
Stays put. The point of the rename is that kit/ is the core; moving it would defeat the rename.
Stays put. Content authored against the kit; doesn't belong inside the toolchain.
Stays put. Demo projects using the kit.
Repo-level entry point. Stays at root.

blocks.title: Config overrides that come with the move
blocks.lead: Each row is a tool that needs to be told ‘the source dir is cli/, not src/’.

rows: Run as ‘uv tool install ./cli’ (path is now cli/, not .)
working-directory: cli on every step that touches Python
Per-IDE preset (.idea/, .vscode/) marks cli/ as Sources
Adjust the inline-script project hint if any path is hard-coded

blocks.title: Cost accepted
blocks.content: These are all one-time edits in known files. Once committed, they're invisible. The recurring cost is ‘uv tool install ./cli’ instead of ‘uv tool install .’ — surfaced in the README and the CI workflow, two places.

blocks.title: Migration — one branch, several commits
blocks.lead: Each step independently passes tests + html-doc check, so the branch can be merged after any single step if something blocks the next.

steps.title: git mv src/ cli/
steps.content: Pure rename — preserves git blame. Update pyproject.toml's [tool.hatch] / [tool.ruff] / [tool.pytest.ini_options] paths to ‘cli/…’ in the same commit so the suite is green at HEAD.

steps.title: Move pyproject.toml + uv.lock into cli/
steps.content: After the move, hatchling configs become relative-to-cli/. README updates: ‘uv tool install ./cli’, ‘cd cli && uv sync --extra dev’. CI workflows gain ‘working-directory: cli’ on every Python step.

steps.title: Move bin/html-doc into cli/bin/
steps.content: Update README + CLAUDE.md examples that show ‘uv run bin/html-doc …’ → ‘uv run cli/bin/html-doc …’. Verify the PEP 723 inline-script header doesn't depend on a top-level path (it shouldn't).

steps.title: Update docs that reference src/
steps.content: grep -ri ‘src/’ docs/ → fix each. CLAUDE.md ‘Top-level files’ table gets rewritten. README ‘Develop’ section gets the new commands.

steps.title: (optional) symlink src → cli for one release
steps.content: If outside tooling (CI presets, package indexes) cache the old layout, a top-level ‘src’ symlink pointing to ‘cli’ buys one release of grace. Skip if no consumer needs it.

blocks.title: Risks — acknowledged + accepted
blocks.lead: Each was a reason the previous draft argued against the rename. Reframed as accepted costs.

cards.title: IDE / editor heuristics
items: PyCharm/VS Code auto-mark src/ as ‘Sources Root’. With cli/, the user marks it manually (one click).
Cost: a one-time IDE setup step per machine.
Accepted: the clarity win for every reader is paid for by a one-click step for two contributors.

cards.title: ‘uv tool install .’ no longer works
items: Becomes ‘uv tool install ./cli’.
Surfaced in README + a one-line note in CLAUDE.md.
Accepted: explicit > implicit. The path now matches what's inside it.

cards.title: GitHub repo-language detection
items: With pyproject.toml under cli/, GitHub may show the repo as JavaScript-first (kit/ has more LoC).
Accurate reflection of the truth: kit IS the core; JS lines >> Python lines.
Accepted: classification matches reality.

cards.title: Wheel install path unchanged
items: Package name stays html_doc; ‘import html_doc’ keeps working downstream.
Only the on-disk source location moves; users of the wheel see no change.
Mitigation: no mitigation needed — wheel consumers are unaffected.

rows: Should src/ symlink to cli/ for one release?
No — the rename is a clean break. Symlink only if CI / a consumer specifically breaks.
External tooling explicitly fails on the move.
Should html_doc_tests/ split out of cli/html_doc/ into cli/tests/?
Yes — Python standard is tests outside the package dir. Sequence as a follow-up commit after the main move.
Wheel sharing test files becomes a real footgun (it already is — minor).
Should cli.py itself be split (~2400 lines today)?
Separate plan. Not blocking the rename.
cli.py crosses ~3000 lines or a non-CLI front-end gets added.
Naming nit: cli vs tools vs toolchain?
A non-CLI front-end joins (then ‘tools/’ might be the umbrella with ‘tools/cli/’, ‘tools/server/’ inside).
What about the ‘html-doc’ CLI binary name itself?
Lives in [[naming]] — separate plan; if the kit is renamed, ‘html-doc’ becomes ‘<newname>’ and bin/html-doc becomes bin/<newname>.
Naming plan lands and triggers the rename of cli/bin/html-doc → cli/bin/<newname>.
